title: Experimental study of fasteners as a delamination arrest mechanism in composite laminates under mode I loading
author: Giovanni Bastiani
abstract: The use of composite materials in several structural applications has been increasing over the past few years due to the fact that these materials have excellent resistance-to-weight and stiffness-to-weight ratios. In the aeronautical industry, carbon fibre-reinforced epoxy laminates have been widely used for the primary and secondary structures of the most modern military and commercial aircraft. Although the use of laminates has several advantages, a major concern is failure due to delamination which might occur exclusively in this type of structure. The ply separation reduces the material strength and stiffness, consequently limiting aircraft structural life. One of the possible alternatives for solving this problem is to increase the material resistance to delamination through the use of fasteners. In this context, this paper presents an experimental study of the capability of fasteners to arrest delamination under Mode I in unidirectional carbon-epoxy laminates. Double-Cantilever Beam (DCB) specimens were tested according to the ASTM D5528 in order to characterise mode I interlaminar fracture toughness with the following configuration: (i) specimen with a hole at 20 mm of the initial crack front; (ii) specimen with a hole reinforced with a conventional bolt and nut without torque (finger tight); (iii) specimen with a hole and a standard aeronautical fastener with half of the nominal torque and (iv) specimen with a hole and a standard aeronautical fastener with nominal torque. The experimental results showed a noticeable capability of fasteners to arrest delamination under Mode I, with an increase in the material resistance occurring even before the crack reaches the fastener. The higher the applied torque, the greater the resistance to delamination due to the more effective crack closing caused by the fastener. Further analysis performed in ultrasound equipment revealed that the crack does not penetrate the fastener but it extends along the sides of the fasteners forming a V-shaped crack front.
